subtitle: Cross-reading for 3 September 2026, the day's second reading: [Polymarket](/en/glossary#polymarket) price from the confirmed reading of 03/Sep, 17:28 BRT (20:28 UTC), presidential book at USD 142.36M, against the PoderData poll of 03/Sep (BR-07561/2026, field 30/Aug to 02/Sep, n=3,000, margin of 2pp), the only national poll with published figures this Thursday. ⭐ A SINGLE CONTRACT MOVED SINCE THE 15:22 READING, and it moved 2.15pp: the runner-up went from 40.35% to 42.50% and the other eighteen stayed flat, with the gap to the leader falling to 12.00pp. 🔴 AND THIS ROUND CORRECTS THE PREVIOUS ONE on Augusto Cury's jump: he was measured into double digits by FOUR houses since 31/Aug, not two, and the first was BTG/[Nexus](/en/glossary#nexus-btg), not Genial/[Quaest](/en/glossary#quaest).

candidates.name: Lula
candidates.header: PRICE: 54.50% (vol USD 9.63M accumulated), confirmed reading of 03/Sep, 17:28 BRT (20:28 UTC), unchanged since today's 15:22 reading. His contract took in about USD 7.0 thousand of new business over that stretch and did not move. POLL: the PoderData poll of 03/Sep (BR-07561/2026, field 30/Aug to 02/Sep, n=3,000, margin of 2pp) gives him 37% in the [first round](/en/glossary#primeiro-turno) and 44% in a [second round](/en/glossary#segundo-turno) in which the runner-up has 45%. He wins the other three pairings the house tested: 44% to 42% against Ronaldo Caiado, 44% to 42% against Romeu Zema and 44% to 39% against Renan Santos.
fortes: He is still ahead in the first round, with 37% against 34% for the runner-up, and the 3-point gap is the same one PoderData itself measured on 27/Aug.
He wins three of the four second-round pairings the house tested, two of them by 2 points and one by 5.
His price did not give ground in the two hours in which the runner-up's rose 2.15pp.

He declared the [INSS](/en/glossary#inss) queue cleared at a ceremony at the Planalto Palace, and requests running more than 45 days late fell 86% since January, from 1.88 million to 261 thousand in August, according to Metrópoles and Poder360.
The lower house approved a provisional measure this Thursday to speed up INSS benefit reviews, according to Metrópoles.
fracos: ⚠️ IN PODERDATA'S SECOND ROUND HE APPEARS BEHIND, 44% to 45%, for the first time in the three rounds from this house since 13/Aug.
His gap to the runner-up in the price fell to 12.00pp, against 16.55pp on 01/Sep, and it narrowed without him moving in this reading.
In the first round he gave ground within the house for the second round running, from 41% on 13/Aug to 38% on 27/Aug and 37% now.

⚠️ THE INSS ANNOUNCEMENT COMES WITH A STATED CRITERION THAT NARROWS WHAT IT MEANS: according to the social security minister, the queue counts as cleared when fewer people are waiting than the number who filed the previous month, and 261 thousand requests past 45 days remain open in August, alongside 1.2 million applications still in progress.
In the first-round runner-up contract he gave up 0.05pp and stands at 8.70%.
candidates.analise: Between today's two readings he did not move, and he still lost ground. His contract took in more new money than his opponent's, about USD 7.0 thousand against about USD 5.8 thousand, and stayed flat at 54.50% while the other rose 2.15pp. The gap between the two fell to 12.00pp, the fourth consecutive timestamp in which it narrows, counting 16.55pp on 01/Sep, 14.85pp on 02/Sep and 14.15pp at 15:22 today. In declared voting intention the picture has not changed since the morning, because there was no new national poll. What changes on his side is the INSS: the ceremony took place, and the definition the government uses to say the queue is cleared is the minister's, with 261 thousand requests past 45 days still open in August.

candidates.name: Flávio Bolsonaro
candidates.header: PRICE: 42.50% (vol USD 9.59M accumulated), confirmed reading of 03/Sep, 17:28 BRT (20:28 UTC), up 2.15pp on today's 15:22 reading, and it is the ONLY move in the presidential book across the two hours between the readings. The gap to the leader fell to 12.00pp. POLL: the PoderData poll of 03/Sep (BR-07561/2026, field 30/Aug to 02/Sep, n=3,000, margin of 2pp) gives him 34% in the first round and 45% in a second round against the leader, who has 44%.
fortes: ⭐ HE WAS THE ONLY NAME IN THE PRESIDENTIAL BOOK TO MOVE BETWEEN TODAY'S TWO READINGS, up 2.15pp, while the other eighteen stayed flat.
The gap to the leader fell to 12.00pp, against 14.15pp at 15:22 today, 14.85pp on 02/Sep and 16.55pp on 01/Sep.
In PoderData's second round he appears numerically ahead, 45% to 44%, for the first time in the three rounds from this house since 13/Aug.
The stock exchange rose 3.06% on 02/Sep after the Genial/Quaest release, according to Metrópoles, and the panel records the sequence without assigning it a cause.
fracos: ⚠️ THE MONEY BEHIND THE RISE IS SMALL: his contract took in about USD 5.8 thousand of new business between today's two readings, less than the roughly USD 7.0 thousand that went into the leader's contract, which did not move.
In the first round he gave ground within PoderData itself, from 35% on 13/Aug and 35% on 27/Aug to 34% now.
The 1-point lead in the second round sits inside the declared margin of 2pp, and the house from the day before measured the same pairing the other way, 41% to 42%.
In the first-round runner-up contract he did not move and is still at 85.50%, meaning the rise stayed entirely in the winner contract.
candidates.analise: The 17:28 reading belongs to him and to nobody else. Between today's two captures the presidential book had a single contract in motion, and it was his, up 2.15pp. What qualifies that move is the money: about USD 5.8 thousand of new business, less than went into the leader's contract, which stayed flat. It is the same caveat the panel applies to the Supreme Court contract, and it applies here because the magnitude is the same. In declared voting intention nothing changed since the morning, and what supports his reading is still PoderData, which puts him numerically ahead in the second round for the first time in the house's three rounds. In the first round, at the same time, he gave up 1 point within that same house.

candidates.name: Augusto Cury
candidates.header: PRICE: 1.35% (vol USD 3.64M accumulated) in the WINNER contract, confirmed reading of 03/Sep, 17:28 BRT (20:28 UTC), unchanged since today's 15:22 reading. In the first-round THIRD-PLACE contract, which is a different market, he rose 0.05pp and stands at 55.90%, in a book of 108 thousand dollars accumulated. POLL: 🔴 THIS ROUND CORRECTS THE PREVIOUS ONE. His jump into double digits was measured by FOUR houses since 31/Aug, not two: BTG/Nexus on 31/Aug at 11%, against 2% in the same house’s round of 24/Aug; Real Time Big Data on 01/Sep at 11%; Genial/Quaest on 02/Sep at 10%, against 2% on 14/Aug and 1% on 05/Aug; and PoderData on 03/Sep at 10%, against 4% on 27/Aug.
fortes: ⭐ FOUR HOUSES MEASURED HIM IN DOUBLE DIGITS SINCE 31/Aug, and three of them have their own series showing the jump: BTG/Nexus on 31/Aug at 11%, against 2% in the same house’s round of 24/Aug; Real Time Big Data on 01/Sep at 11%; Genial/Quaest on 02/Sep at 10%, against 2% on 14/Aug and 1% on 05/Aug; and PoderData on 03/Sep at 10%, against 4% on 27/Aug. AtlasIntel on 31/Aug measured him at 7.8%.
The largest jump between two consecutive rounds of the same house, in this window, is BTG/Nexus: from 2% on 24/Aug to 11% on 31/Aug, seven days between the two rounds.
In the first-round third-place contract he leads with 55.90% and rose 0.05pp in this reading, after 3.45pp in the previous one.
His rejection rate is 25% in the Genial/Quaest poll of 02/Sep, the lowest among the seven most prominent names tested, against 55% for the runner-up and 53% for the leader.
In the first-round runner-up contract he rose 0.30pp and stands at 2.45% (vol USD 124 thousand).
fracos: ⚠️ THE TWO CONTRACTS STILL POINT IN OPPOSITE DIRECTIONS, and the winner contract did not react to the jump: it stands at 1.35% and has not moved since the 15:22 reading, while declared voting intention puts him at 10% or 11% across four houses.
The 1.35% in the winner contract sits alongside double digits in declared voting intention. It is the widest gap between poll and price in the table.

The PoderData poll of 03/Sep did NOT test a [second round](/en/glossary#segundo-turno) with him, so the only second-round reading in the base is still the Genial/Quaest one of 02/Sep, in which he loses to the leader by 40% to 34%.
Accumulated volume in his winner contract is USD 3.64M, the smallest among the seven names in the table.
The campaigns of the other candidates outside the top two sharpened their tone against him after the jump, according to O Globo.
candidates.analise: His case changed size in this round, and through an error of ours. The 15:22 reading said the jump had been measured by two houses and that Genial/Quaest of 02/Sep was the first. Both claims were wrong, and the readings that disprove them were already in the panel's file: four houses measured him in double digits, and the first was BTG/Nexus on 31/Aug, four days earlier. With the base corrected, the reading gets firmer rather than weaker: three houses show the jump within their own series, and the largest jump between consecutive rounds is from 2% to 11% in seven days. In the price, none of that showed up in the winner contract, which is still at 1.35% and did not move in the two hours between today's readings. The market priced the jump into the third-place contract, where he leads with 55.90%, and not into the winner contract. They are different questions, and the answer changes with the question.

fracos: In the first-round third-place contract he gave up 0.50pp and now stands at 26.50%, against 55.90% for the leader, and the gap keeps widening.
In the first round he gave ground within the house, from 4% on 27/Aug to 3%, over the same interval in which Augusto Cury went from 4% to 10%.

candidates.analise: He is the name the houses disagree on most in this window, and that matters more than any single reading of him: in the panel's base the figures run from 3% at Genial/Quaest and PoderData to 6% at Real Time and 7.6% at AtlasIntel. In the second round against the leader, though, the margin against him narrowed from 7 to 5 points within the house. In the price this round reads as stillness in the winner contract and a 0.50pp fall in the third-place contract, where he was overtaken on 01/Sep and the gap to the leader keeps widening.

cruzamento: The day's second reading measures two things, and the first is a correction of our own. 🔴 AUGUSTO CURY'S JUMP INTO DOUBLE DIGITS WAS MEASURED BY FOUR HOUSES, NOT TWO, and it began on 31/Aug and not this Thursday. In the panel's base: BTG/Nexus on 31/Aug at 11%, against 2% in the same house’s round of 24/Aug; Real Time Big Data on 01/Sep at 11%; Genial/Quaest on 02/Sep at 10%, against 2% on 14/Aug and 1% on 05/Aug; and PoderData on 03/Sep at 10%, against 4% on 27/Aug. AtlasIntel on 31/Aug measured him at 7.8%. This page's 15:22 reading said two houses and named Genial/Quaest as the first, and both claims were wrong: all four readings were already in our own file, and the within-house comparison shows the jump in three of them, with BTG/Nexus going from 2% to 11% in seven days. The second thing is the price. ⭐ A SINGLE CONTRACT IN THE PRESIDENTIAL BOOK MOVED IN TWO HOURS. The runner-up rose 2.15pp, from 40.35% to 42.50%, and the other eighteen names stayed flat, the leader included, who is still at 54.50%. The gap between the two fell to 12.00pp, against 14.15pp in today's 15:22 reading, 14.85pp on 02/Sep and 16.55pp on 01/Sep. ⚠️ AND THE MONEY BEHIND IT IS SMALL: between today's two readings the runner-up's contract took in about USD 5.8 thousand of new business and the leader's took in about USD 7.0 thousand without moving, in a book that has accumulated USD 142.36M. Because the runner-up rose and no one else gave ground, the sum of the YES legs across the 19 contracts went from 99.20% to 101.35%. ⚠️ THIS IS NOT AN ANOMALY, AND IT WAS CHECKED IN THE SERIES BACKUP: summing only the four names above the 0.5% floor, which is the quantity the series stores, the total went from 97.95% to 100.10%, and across the 20 previous captures that same sum ranged from 98.00% to 101.60%, with 13 of them above 100%. Above 100 is this book's ordinary behaviour. The rule the panel already applies to the [Supreme Court](/en/glossary#stf) contract applies here in the same way: a price that moves a lot on very little money does not describe a shift in expectations of the same size. In the polls nothing changed since 15:22, and [Datafolha](/en/glossary#datafolha), scheduled for release today on the [TSE](/en/glossary#tse) register, still had no figures at the time of this reading.
